title: Kernel-checked results on the Riemann Hypothesis: de Bruijn-Newman bounds and a conditional Riemann-Roch-square criterion
description: Lean 4 formalizations, papers and a vendored copy of the Telperion certificate engine, collecting kernel-checked results around the Riemann Hypothesis. The Riemann Hypothesis is open and is not proved here. Unconditional: 0 <= Lambda <= 0.2811857 for the de Bruijn-Newman constant (dbn_newman along Dobner's proof, selberg_newman and selberg_newman_sharp for the extended Selberg class, dbn_real_zeros_of_qrh_unconditional from OpenAI's quasi-Riemann hypothesis, dbn_real_zeros_ge_2811857 from Baiying Liu's half-plane), each judged by Comparator with nanoda; pole-free one-prime Weil positivity for test functions supported in [-0.5493, 0.5493] (Hodge1.weil_positivity_poleFree2_window5493). Equivalences and conditional results: RH iff Weil positivity on pole-free tests (RvMBridgePF.rh_iff_poleFree_weil_positivity); RH iff that positivity for tests not supported in the window (Hodge1.rh_iff_poleFree2_outside_window5493); and the Riemann-Roch-square criterion: a family of RR-square windows covering every pole-free test implies RH (RvMBridgePF.rh_of_rr_windows), and conversely RH gives such windows trivially (RvMBridgePF.rh_iff_exists_rr_windows), so all content is a construction without reference to the zeros, together with the abstract Hodge-index theorems, a countermodel and function-field instances. No RR-square family is constructed. All theorems depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. OpenAI's and Liu's code is fetched at pinned commits and not redistributed. Not refereed. v1.0.2 updates only the bundled copy of the Telperion engine; the three papers are unchanged. It fixes three defects found by an independent AI audit, not by human review: (1) Telperion's winding-number zero counts (the default backend of the winding_box_zero emitter) were evaluated only at sample points on each box's edge; they are now rigorous in Arb interval arithmetic (not kernel-checked). (2) The Davenport–Heilbronn inventory missed a fifth off-line zero below height 300, ρ ≈ 0.86953 + 240.40467i, because the off-line scan its documentation promised had never been written; the zero is now added and the inventory is proved complete (214 = 204 + 2·5). (3) The Báez-Duarte emitter's old family carried a false "RH ⟺ d²→0" label; it now uses Bagchi's family. Every previously certified box was re-checked with the rigorous method and remains correct, including the box counts on which Lean hypotheses such as those in ZooDH rest. No theorem in the papers or progress record depended on any of these defects. See CHANGELOG.md. Licensing: mathematics Apache-2.0, papers and prose CC-BY-4.0, Telperion engine BSL 1.1.
